Finding ownership in nested systems

Deeply nested markup does not necessarily imply deeply nested responsibility. The useful question is which module owns the behavior and which interface a caller must understand.

When transaction policy leaks through several layers, every caller learns database details. Moving that policy behind one durable command interface reduces the facts that handlers and application logic need to coordinate.

Tests should cross the same seam as production callers. Internal adapters can still be replaced for fault injection without exposing their mechanics in the external interface.
